text:
Sasha: quick heads-up — ran a 4h evening sweep on prod GPUs, saw a recurring p95 blip around 1200ms on short-chat traces. looks like prefill is fine but decode tails spike when KV miss rate > 6% :grimacing:
Arjun: ugh. do we know if it's kernel-switching overhead or batching slowdown?
Maya: profiler traces point to a few hotspots: kernel selection + small microbatch assembly (~2-6 tokens) + extra memcpy when KV fallback happens. attached snippet from perf-bot earlier:
perf-bot: CPU samples:
```
# top stacks
runtime_scheduler -> choose_kernel_by_shape -> launch_kernel -> memcpy_sync
attention_kernel_shortseq -> handle_kv_miss -> fallback_prepare
```

Eli: that memcpy_sync smells like prefilling the KV into host memory when miss occurs. iirc we only do that on cold misses. but with microbatches of size 1-2 we sometimes pay that cost in the decode path.
Sasha: agreed. thoughts on priorities? my vote: 1) avoid kernel churn for short decodes (force stable kernel if seq_len < 64 and batch < 8), 2) add a tiny prefill-only warmup probe to reduce KV misses on tail, 3) tweak microbatch cap when we detect high KV miss rate.
Arjun: love the ranked list. one caveat: forcing kernel might slightly increase avg latency for some mid-lengths. need an experiment to measure p50 vs p99 tradeoff.
Maya: i sketched an AB plan:
- variant A: kernel-lock for short-path (seq<64 && batch<=8)
- variant B: adaptive microbatcher that raises min-batch to 4 when kv_miss_rate > 3%
- control: current scheduling
measure p50/p95/p99 + token-cost delta over 24h.
Sasha: put the rollout as a canary on a single pool (gpu-pool-3). also add a flag to the scheduler to log kernel-choice events (compact format):
```
KERNEL_EVENT seq=23 batch=1 chosen=attn_short prev=auto reason=lock
KV_EVENT miss=true latency_ms=8 handled=host_copy
```

Eli: for the KV warmup probe — propose a lightweight prefix probe that runs only when route is cold (no recent hits) and is sized to match the typical prefix length (16-32 tokens). we should throttle it aggressively: max 1 probe/min per model+route.
Arjun: also worth exploring an optimized memcpy path: async device->device staging instead of host copy on common HW we run. that could shave 3-5ms on the hot path. but requires a kernel-side change.
Maya: timeline suggestion: put kernel-lock experiment in today (quick config), microbatcher change next week, kv-probe + memcpy optimization as follow-ups. can someone own the memcpy spike analysis?
Sasha: I'll take memcpy follow-up. Eli can prototype the kv-probe. Arjun + Maya pair on the AB and canary metrics.
perf-bot: perf-alert: pool gpu-pool-3 p99 decode increased by +18% between 2323452000-2323455600, kv_miss_rate jumped to 7.1%
Sasha: perfect — that perf-alert gives us a target window for the canary. one more ask: in the experiment logs, include per-request "prefill_time_ms" and "decode_time_ms" fields so we can attribute changes. without that split the signal is noisy.
Eli: agree — i'll add those fields to the tracer. quick sampling format:
```
TRACE req_id=... prefill_time_ms=24 decode_time_ms=103 kernel=attn_short kv_hit=true
```

Maya: ok codewise i'll add the kernel-lock flag behind a runtime config and a metric that counts kernel-lock hits. will also emit a small histogram of microbatch sizes.
Arjun: if kernel-lock reduces tail but increases avg cost >3% we should gate it behind "cost-neutral" rule in rollout (auto rollback).
Sasha: ok deploy plan: config-only canary today -> 2% traffic on gpu-pool-3 for 4h -> collect p50/p95/p99 + token-cost + kv_miss_rate. if p99 improves and cost delta < +2%, expand to 20% and enable microbatcher variant.
Eli: noted. i'll add dashboards and an alert rule for kv_miss_rate > 5% during the canary window.
Maya: cool. i'll open a lightweight PR with the config toggle + logging. keeping changes small so we can iterate fast.
Sasha: thanks team. we should reconvene after the 4h canary to decide next steps. :thumbsup:
